decision.topic: what a changed DATA file should do to a tab
decision.question: A path the tab fetched as data changed. Reload, or tell the page?
options: reload the tab (what it did)
hot-swap it like CSS
emit a page-level event the page subscribes to
decision.why: A data file cannot be hot-swapped — nothing in the DOM points at it, the page READ it. But a change to it is new CONTENT, not new code: the program in the browser is byte-identical afterwards, so re-reading the file is the whole fix. Socket now fires socket.on("data", path) for a path whose resource entry says fetch/xhr AND whose extension is .json/.jsonl/.md/.txt/.csv. Both tests are needed: ext/files FETCHES a .js to show its source, and that same .js is a live module that really does need a reload.

decision.question: Which consumer subscribes to the new data event?
options: ext/AITask/dashboard.js (the AI boards)
core/Page's router
ext/Omnibox, ext/Search and the rest
decision.chose: public/framework/ext/AITask/dashboard.js — one helper, on_directory(), called from dashboard() (the day board) and rail() (the ai index)
decision.why: core/Page's router never reads directory.json; ext/AITask is the only consumer the owner actually sits in front of while agents work, and it is where a new task dir has to appear. Both call sites were one line each on top of a redraw path the module already had. The other consumers (Omnibox, Search, Doc, Research, Panel/Workspace) fetch it once on open and are not long-lived boards — they can adopt the same one-liner when someone wants them live.

decision.question: Should a blocked tab still hot-swap CSS and fire data events?
options: no — blocked means nothing happens at all (the old behaviour, documented in dev/Socket/doc/method/changed.md)
yes — only the reload itself is refused
decision.chose: only the reload itself is refused
decision.why: Blocking means "do not throw my state away". A CSS swap and a data re-read throw nothing away — they are exactly what the reader wanted instead of a reload. It also makes the skipped counter honest: it now counts reloads that would really have happened, not every batch that arrived. dev/Socket/doc/method/changed.md updated to match.

decision.topic: restoring a fold across a reload
decision.question: How do you put back the open card the brief asks for?
options: re-add the `open` class to whatever had it
stamp a data-reload-keep attribute as an opt-in seam
native <details open> only, and say plainly what cannot be done
decision.why: ext/AITask's fold() BUILDS ITS BODY ON FIRST CLICK. Re-adding its `open` class after a reload would show an open, empty box — worse than a shut one — and an opt-in attribute has exactly the same problem. Native <details> is safe because its content is always in the DOM. ?view= and #hash need nothing: the url survives a reload by itself. Written into Socket.js beside the code.

assign.outcome:
**A tab now reloads only when something it RUNS changed — 215 reloads a day became 12.**

You were right that it was reloading for the wrong reason. On 2026-09-22 a tab left open on the AI board reloaded **215 times**, and **203 of those (94%) were `directory.json`** — the list of what is on disk, rebuilt every time any agent created any file anywhere under `public/`. The board had *read* that file. Nothing it was *running* had changed.

The rule now: a file a page **reads** is content, a file a page **runs** is code, and only code needs a reload. A changed data file fires `socket.on("data", path)` and the page re-reads it in place.

**[Read the answer to "do we even need live reload?"](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/reload-rethink/)** — one screen, detail one click down.

**The four proofs, all on a real headless browser against a real server:**

- **A new task dir does not move the page.** Navigation count **0**; the day board's count goes "Proposed — 2 not started" to "3" in **653ms**.
- **A reload that IS needed keeps your place.** Scrolled 1,500px into a 5,444px page, touched a running module, it reloaded and landed at **1,500px — 0px out**. (⚠ `window.scrollY` is always 0 on this site; `.pages` is the scroller. Stashing `scrollY` would have restored nothing while looking like it worked.)
- **The dev bar's `block` switch is yours now** — per tab, remembered for the life of the tab, and it shows "3 held"; clicking that takes the held reloads in one go. Counted 0 to 1 to 2 across two changes that would each have reloaded the tab.
- **Worktrees never reach you.** A real worktree, a real edit inside it: **0** paths from it ever appeared on the main server's wire — while in the same four seconds that server broadcast 4 paths from another agent working live, so it was not a silent wire.

**Still needs a reload, and cannot be helped without a build step:** a changed ES module. The browser cannot re-import one over the old copy; re-importing with `?t=` gives you a *second* copy running beside the first, which is worse. That is now most of what a reload is for.

**Also found and fixed:** `dev/DevBar/hold.js` — the "held by <who>, 12s" readout built three days ago — was never called from anywhere, so it had never once appeared on screen. Wired in.

**Left, in one line each:**

- `ai/health/devbar.js` has the same problem and is still dark — one line in `DevBar.js` would light it, but the module is not mine.
- `Server/worktree-down.mjs` cannot clean its own registry entry once the directory is gone; it tells you to edit `.worktrees.json` by hand (I did).
- Only the AI boards subscribe to the new `data` event; Omnibox, Search, Doc and Research still fetch `directory.json` once on open, which is correct for what they are.
- The census reconstruction is from file mtimes — `LiveReload` now logs `[reload] <n paths> … → <n> sockets told` so nobody has to do that again.

**Docs:** [changed()](/framework/dev/Socket/api/changed/) · [on()](/framework/dev/Socket/api/on/) · [DevBar](/framework/dev/DevBar/) · [the superseded "block stores nothing" decision](/framework/dev/DevBar/doc/decisions/)

decision.topic: how a hold stops being global
decision.question: The owner's save did not reload the owner's tab while a minion held. Where does the fence live?
options: LiveReload decides per socket (hold only tabs the holder's own server serves)
the holder declares --paths and LiveReload partitions its queue against them
shorten the TTL so a global hold hurts less
decision.chose: the holder declares --paths; LiveReload partitions its queue on every flush
decision.why: A per-socket rule cannot work — every tab is on the same server and the server cannot know which tab the owner is sitting in. A shorter TTL treats a wrong shape as a timing problem, and the owner would still lose reloads for 30s at a time. The holder is the only party that knows what it is about to write, which is exactly what its brief's fence already says, so asking it to declare that costs nothing and makes the hold say something true. flush() used to open with `if (held) return;` and now splits the queue: inside a live fence stays queued, everything else goes out at once.

decision.topic: the default fence for a hold that names none
decision.question: Every existing caller passes no --paths. What do they hold?
options: everything, as before
nothing — refuse a fenceless hold
public/framework/ai/** plus a warning naming the holder
decision.chose: public/framework/ai/** plus a warning naming the holder
decision.why: The brief's own answer, and the right one: the boards are where agents really write in bulk (every new-task makes a dir, every append lands a file), so it covers the real case, while deliberately NOT covering the rest of the site — so the owner editing a page still sees their own save even when an agent forgot. Refusing outright would have broken every caller in flight, including the hold-guard hook, at the moment the change landed.

log.msg: D7 PROOFS, 10/10, headless on a private server (8097). THE HOLD: with `d7-proof` holding ai/v/3/** the tab on /framework/ai2/ reloaded 540ms after its own file changed — the owner's exact scenario, now working — while a change under ai/v/3/ reached NO tab at all over 4s, and releasing the hold flushed 3 v/3 paths at once. The DEFAULT fence: a hold with no --paths holds only ai/** and prints a warning naming the holder, and even then a save outside the boards still reloads. THE READOUT: silent and zero-height when free; "board-declutter holds ai/v/3/**, 1s" on screen when held; the full fence plus "Everything outside these fences still reloads normally" in the tooltip; a fenceless holder flagged as such; quiet again on release.

The glob language is unit-tested before anything used it, 12 cases: ai/** matches ai/v/3/v3.css and does NOT match ai2/page.js (the exact discrimination the proof needs), ** crosses slashes and * does not, a pattern with no wildcard is a directory prefix (ai/v/3 covers ai/v/3/v3.css but not ai/v/33/x.css), and repo-relative, ./-prefixed and url-path inputs all normalise to the same thing. matches() in Server/hold.mjs is the only implementation; LiveReload imports it rather than reimplementing.

TWO TRAPS FOUND WHILE BUILDING IT. (1) Bash expands an unquoted `**` before node sees it — my first `--paths public/framework/dev/DevBar/**` arrived as 19 enumerated filenames. Harmless here but not what was written, so the CLI usage, Server/README.md, the minion skill and the report all say QUOTE THE GLOBS. (2) The hold-guard hook renews a lapsed hold with `add(who, what, ttl)` and no paths, which would have silently widened a holder back to the default fence on every renewal — a hold getting BIGGER while nobody looks is the same class of bug as the global hold. add() now keeps the previous fence when a renewal passes none, so the hook needed no change.

THIRD TEST-BUG OF THE RUN, same lesson: the "named no --paths" warning is a console.warn, so it goes to stderr, and execFileSync returns only stdout — my assertion read an empty stream and reported FAIL against working code. Switched to spawnSync and joined both streams. Kept the warning on stderr: that is the right channel for a warning, and an agent running the CLI through the Bash tool sees both.

A sibling agent rewrote the minion skill's reload-hold section while I was fixing the thing it describes, so it stated the bug as current ("a held server blocks the OWNER's own saves from reloading their own tab"). Corrected in place to past tense with the fix named, and my --paths form merged under it rather than over it. Left intact: that agent's own lead — work in a worktree first, hold for seconds not minutes — which is still exactly right.

You saw it yourself: your dev bar said *"held by board-declutter, 220 seconds"* and your own save did not reload your own tab. ```

**Proved headless, 10/10**, with that exact hold on:
